correctness.rationale: The exact restriction of the cone polynomial to the two-dimensional Grassmannian-chart pencil yields four coefficient equations. The nonzero (x,y) coordinates permit elimination of u,v via u=y^q w,v=-x^q w; the remaining ideal is (P w^q,w^(q+1)) over the smooth Hermitian curve, P=xy^(q²)-yx^(q²). Its zero locus equals F_(q²)-points and dP on the curve tangent is -1, so t=P is a uniformizer; exact primary decomposition (tw^q,w^(q+1))=(w^q) intersection (t,w^(q+1)) gives embedded length one, generic length q and special transverse length q+1. Norm-fiber counting gives q^3+1. Explicit finite q=2 independent F4 enumeration found six affine plus three infinite Hermitian points and verified the Frobenius polynomial vanishes; universal result follows from algebraic proof, not enumeration.
